Sure, here is a detailed description of the video segment you provided.

The video shows a tutorial of how to install the Kodi app onto a USB drive. The scene is of a computer screen, and no people are visible. The video segment starts with the narrator opening the “This PC” window on a Windows operating system. The window displays various folders and drives, including the USB drive. The narrator right-clicks on the USB drive and selects “Format” from the context menu. A “Format USB Drive” window appears, and the narrator clicks the “Start” button. A pop-up warns that formatting will erase all data on the disk, and the narrator clicks “OK” to confirm. After formatting is complete, the narrator clicks “OK” again to close the message. Then the narrator opens the Kodi file on the desktop and runs the executable file (kodi-16.1-Jarvis.exe). Then the narrator clicks “Next”, “Agree”, then “Next” again. Then he clicks “Browse” to show the location to install the application, then clicks on USB drive (I), and clicks OK to confirm. Finally, the narrator clicks “Next” and “Install”. The narrator is explaining the process of using a USB drive to install Kodi and take the application anywhere. The backdrop of the desktop shows a road through green mountains.

The video shows a computer screen displaying the installation process of Kodi software. The setup window, titled "Kodi Setup," indicates that Kodi is being installed with a progress bar showing the extraction of various files. The progress information updates, indicating the percentage of completion. The text "Installing: Please wait while Kodi is being installed" is visible at the top of the window. At the bottom of the window, there are buttons labeled "Back", "Next", and "Cancel". Below the progress bar, there is also a button labeled "Show details." As the installation progresses, the screen transitions to the "Completing the Kodi Setup Wizard" screen, informing that Kodi has been installed. The final window also contains the Kodi logo, a checkbox to "Run Kodi," and a "Finish" button at the bottom. The desktop background displays a highway scene with cars.

The video segment displays a desktop screen running Windows, where the user interacts with files and windows. At the start of the segment, the Kodi Setup window is displayed, indicating that Kodi has been installed. The user clicks on the "Finish" button. The focus then shifts to the file explorer window, which navigates to the user's USB drive (Drive L:) and opens the "Kodi" folder, which contains various Kodi-related files including "Kodi.exe". Following this, the user right-clicks on the desktop and selects "New," then "Shortcut". A window then pops up, asking the user to "Type the location of the item."

The video segment displays a computer screen showing a "Create Shortcut" wizard window. The user navigates a folder selection dialogue box within the wizard, expanding the USB Drive (I:) directory and then the "Kodi" folder within. They then select the "Kodi.exe" file, which is highlighted and described as an "Application," with a size of "19.8 MB" and "Date modified: 24/04/2016 10:30." After pressing 'OK,' the wizard displays the path 'I:\Kodi\Kodi.exe' in a text box where the user then adds " -p" (space hyphen p). Below the prompt "Click Next to continue," the user clicks "Next." The final wizard step is shown, which displays the default shortcut name "Kodi.exe," and provides the prompt "Click Finish to create the shortcut," after which the video ends. There is a blurred background with vertical lines, that appears to be a busy highway.

The video segment starts with a file directory window on a desktop displaying various files and their properties, including the Kodi.exe file. The speaker says that they want to create a portable version of the Kodi executable file. Then they proceed to open the Kodi.exe file. Upon opening, a "portable_data" folder appears in the directory. Next, the screen transitions to the Kodi loading screen, which features the software's logo, tagline, and version number (v16.1 - Jarvis). The screen subsequently transitions to a blue, bubbly, almost abstract visual scene. The segment ends here.

The video segment shows the Kodi interface on a Windows desktop. The main screen displays a blue, bubble-filled background with a horizontal menu bar at the bottom with options like "Pictures," "Videos," "Music," "Programs," and "System." There is text on the screen that says: "Kodi goes Windows Store Kodi v17 'Krypton'". Below that, there are icons for favorite, and power off. The user selects the power off icon, which opens a pop-up window with options: "Exit", "Power off system", "Custom shutdown timer", "Suspend", "Hibernate" and "Reboot". The scene transitions to a Windows desktop showing a file explorer window titled "This PC > USB Drive (I:) > Kodi." The window lists various files and folders related to Kodi, including "addons," "media," "userdata," and "Uninstall.exe". The desktop background displays a high-speed highway at night. The bottom of the screen shows a taskbar with icons for various applications.

The video shows a screencast of a Windows PC screen. The person in the video is demonstrating how to put a build into the "portable_data" folder of Kodi, a media player software. The screen shows two open file explorer windows side by side. The left window shows the file structure of a USB drive, specifically the Kodi folder with files like "addons", "cache", "media", "system", "userdata", and "kodi.log". A progress bar is shown indicating deletion of files and folder in the Kodi Folder. The right window displays the Kodi folder on a desktop containing various Kodi builds for reviews. The person in the video selects "Fresh Copy" and then "addons" and "userdata" file folders and copies them into the "portable_data" folder.  The person is working with files and folders, using drag and drop operations to move data between different locations. The background includes the standard Windows desktop environment with icons, a recycle bin, and a taskbar at the bottom, and the background wallpaper is a scenic view of a winding road at night.

The video shows a person using a Windows PC to copy files, and using the Kodi media player application. Initially, the screen displays a file explorer window copying “730 items from Fresh Copy to portable_data”, and the progress bar shows completion going from 43% to 99% as the presenter talks about the importance of having at least 60 GB of storage on the SD card. Once the copying process is complete, the file explorer is closed, and a desktop with icons for various programs and files appears. The background of the desktop features a scenic landscape with winding roads. Finally, the person opens the Kodi application, displaying the Kodi logo and version information (Kodi v16.1- Jarvis). The Kodi interface is then displayed, initially showing a black background, then the person navigates through Kodi settings to change the background image source to a file on their SD card. With this change made, the background image appears to be a collection of YouTube tutorials.

The video shows a person explaining how to move Kodi from the user's computer to a USB drive. Initially, we see the computer's desktop screen, which is cluttered with various application icons against a scenic wallpaper depicting a mountain road at dusk. The person selects the Kodi shortcut from the desktop, opens the computer's file explorer to access the USB drive (labeled as USB Drive (I:)), and pastes the Kodi shortcut inside the "portable_data" folder. The person then copies the pasted shortcut to the desktop. Subsequently, they launch Kodi, which displays the Kodi logo followed by the Kodi application's interface featuring various options (VIDEOS, PROGRAMS, SYSTEM) along with content from a YouTube channel called "Game of Ohms". This transition demonstrates how Kodi can be run from a USB drive on a new computer without installation. The overall tone is instructional.

The screen capture shows a Kodi interface with the "Videos," "Programs," and "System" options displayed across the middle. Below these options are previews of various video tutorials and add-ons. The top part of the screen shows the "Game of Ohms" YouTube channel interface, displaying the channel's home page with options like "Home," "Videos," "Playlists," and more. A featured video is displayed prominently, along with a description of the DC Sports add-on for Kodi. The text at the bottom informs that "Evolve" is back and available in its dedicated repo, with a link provided. The time is displayed as 7:02 PM on Tuesday, September 27, 2016. Overall, the interface is busy and filled with various elements related to video content, Kodi add-ons, and tutorials.
